subject: Onboarding timeline & pricing clarifications for Orion Health pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding timeline & pricing clarifications for Orion Health pilot

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we discussed, I put together a short sequencing proposal to align the onboarding milestones you care about (test dataset evaluation, performance acceptance, pilot ramp) with commercial triggers so procurement has a coherent path to close.

Attached: Orion_MAP_v1.xlsx (high level sequencing) and a short SOW stub that maps acceptance windows to deliverables.

Key notes / asks from our side:
- Proposed pilot length: 8 weeks (2-week eval + 6-week ramp).
- Pricing during eval: usage discounted 100% up to 100K tokens (trial credit) then standard eval rates thereafter.
- Commit tranche for month 1 of paid pilot: 25% of target monthly tokens; full commit applies after month 2.
- True-ups: quarterly reconciliation based on billable units; we typically offer a 30-day reconciliation window.

Can you confirm whether your procurement team needs: (a) a hard cap on price movement (price protection), (b) a specific true-up cadence other than quarterly, or (c) a different definition of billable usage (e.g., exclude internal system prompts)?

If useful, Ben can join a short call this week to walk through the MAP spreadsheet.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: Orion_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SOW_onboarding_draft.pdf (SOW excerpt)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orionhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Martha Lee <martha.lee@orionhealth.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding timeline & pricing clarifications for Orion Health pilot

Kimberly —

Appreciate the summary and the attachments. A few clarification points from our side before we loop in procurement formally: 

1) True-up cadence: Quarterly is fine, but procurement will push for a 45-day invoice/adjustment window after quarter close — is that something Redwood can support?

2) Price protection: we need a cap on any price increase during the first 12 months to avoid surprise rate changes while we ramp. Is a 3% nominal cap reasonable? If not, what are your standard protections for pilot-to-contract transitions?

3) Definition of billable usage: we want system prompts and orchestration tokens excluded from billable counts where they don’t contribute to customer-visible outputs. Can you confirm if your usage meter can exclude designated prompt tokens?

Also — given our internal procurement timeline, we’re trying to target a contract signature within 60 days from today if the economic terms are acceptable. That would require the MAP and contract draft to be stable within three weeks. Can Ben do an hour to walk through the spreadsheet on Friday?

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Director of Product | Orion Health
alex.turner@orionhealth.com

Alex —

Happy to run through the sequencing. Quick responses inline and a short attached walkthrough:

- 45-day post-quarter reconciliation: we can accommodate a 45-day true-up window; operationally we’ll flag any out-of-band usage and surface it in billing reports.

- Price protection: our standard pilot protection is a 0-5% nominal cap for annualized increases during the first contract year. For pilots under $100k ARR we often do a guaranteed 0% movement during the pilot and then a 3% cap at renewal — but we can be flexible based on commit bands.

- Excluding system/orchestration tokens: we can configure the meter to exclude specific token classes (system prompts / orchestration) as long as they’re clearly annotated in the prompt pipeline. We’ll need a short appendix in the SOW that lists the excluded token markers.

I attached a short walk-through PDF (embedded notes in Orion_MAP_v1.xlsx).

Suggested sequencing to meet your 60-day close target:
1) This week: walkthrough with Ben (30–45m) and finalize MAP spreadsheet.
2) Next week: Neha to circulate a redline-friendly SOW + basic commercial term sheet.
3) Week 3: procurement review + signoff on price protection and true-up language.
4) Week 4–5: sign contract and schedule go-live.

If those windows work, I’ll block Friday 10:00am PT for a walkthrough.

—Ben

Subject: Draft SOW & redline guidance (Orion Health pilot)

Alex / Procurement team —

Following Ben’s sequencing, I’ve attached a draft SOW excerpt and a short summary of the commercial points we expect procurement to confirm. High-level positions below to speed review: 

- True-up cadence: Redwood’s position is quarterly reconciliation with a 45-day invoice/adjustment window (per Ben’s note). We propose a floor adjustment approach: any under-consumption below committed tranches will not trigger retroactive penalties in the pilot period; overages will be invoiced at the agreed usage rate and reconciled at quarter end.

- Price protection: For the initial 12 months post-signature we propose a price movement cap of 3% (nominal). If Orion prefers 0% during the pilot window, we can offer 0% lock for the pilot period (8 weeks) with a 3% cap thereafter to 12 months.

- Usage definition: Billable usage = customer-visible generation tokens + production embeddings called by customer-facing features. System prompts, orchestration control tokens, and internal QA runs excluded if flagged via the token annotation mechanism described in Appendix A. Please flag any orchestration flows that need exemption.

- Audit & reporting: Redwood will provide token-level daily usage reports accessible via the console and a monthly summary export for procurement.

Attachments: SOW_onboarding_draft.pdf (with Appendix A), ChangeSummary_redlines.txt (short list of proposed contract edits).

If procurement sends a short list of must-haves, we can incorporate them into a single redline for efficiency. Happy to take a call with your legal early next week.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Commercial Counsel | Redwood Inference

2) We will take the 0% pricing movement guarantee for the pilot window, then a 3% cap through month 12. Please include that phrasing in the SOW.
3) Usage exclusions: we will provide a short list of orchestration flows to be marked as non-billable.
